open_points.subject: R0-04 / R0-26 context and validate answers
open_points.text: the fields stay, but every read is authenticated and carries the disclosure class of what it returns
open_points.question: The `context` answer carries `address`, which R0-26 makes `personal_data`. A consumer whose token does not allow `personal_data` reads it. Is the read refused, does the field go missing (breaking R0-04's field-for-field contract), or is there a separate projection?
options: refuse context to tokens below personal_data
omit or blank address for those tokens and accept the contract change
keep context unchanged and add a separate non-personal projection
every context consumer's token must allow personal_data
open_points.default_guess: Keep `context` field for field and refuse it to any token that does not allow `personal_data`. Add a separate projection without the address for the other consumers.

open_points.subject: R0-40 retention of archived projects
open_points.text: The object's address and characteristics, and archived projects: five years after the project is closed (archived) ... erased or anonymised
open_points.question: R0-03 and R0-12 say archiving never deletes. R0-06 says customer erasure is the only exception to R0-03. Does R0-40 replace or narrow R0-03 and R0-06? If so, what stays readable by id after a project's period ends?
options: R0-40 adds a second exception to R0-03; the project's id stays readable as anonymised
only the object's personal data is erased; the project record stays
R0-40 does not apply to the project record itself
open_points.default_guess: Name R0-40 as a second exception to R0-03. The project id, its status and its pointers stay readable. The object's address and characteristics are anonymised.

open_points.subject: R0-38 one object per project vs create
open_points.text: A project has exactly one object
open_points.question: 'Create a project' no longer requires an address and does not create an object. Object recording is a separate action. Can a project exist without an object? If it can, what does `context` answer as `address` then?
options: create requires the object (address, kind) in the same request
a project may have zero or one object; context answers a null address
an empty object is created with the project
open_points.default_guess: A project has at most one object. `context` answers `address` as null until the object is recorded.

open_points.subject: correct a project vs record or correct a project's object
open_points.text: the project with the new name, customer or object, next revision
open_points.question: Is the object corrected through 'correct a project', through 'record or correct a project's object', or through both? Which revision does an object change move: the project's, the object's, or both?
options: object only via its own action, with its own revision
object via project correction, with the project revision only
both actions, both revisions move
open_points.default_guess: The object changes only through its own action and moves only its own revision. 'Correct a project' covers name and customer.

open_points.subject: stale-revision checks
open_points.text: A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an older revision is refused
open_points.question: R0-35 covers every change to a project, customer or object. The table lists a stale refusal only for corrections. Do archive, erase and restrict also state a revision and refuse a stale one?
options: yes, every state change of these records
no, only field corrections
open_points.default_guess: Yes. Archive, erase and restrict state a revision and refuse a stale one, except for an idempotent repeat.

open_points.subject: restrict processing of a customer
open_points.text: the Customer marked restricted: its contact data stays stored but leaves Registry to no one but the owner
open_points.question: Can a restriction be lifted? Can a restricted customer be corrected or named by a new project? What does restricting an already restricted customer return?
options: add 'lift restriction' (owner); restriction blocks nothing else
restriction is final until erasure
open_points.default_guess: Add 'lift a restriction' for the owner. Restricting a restricted customer returns it unchanged. Correction and naming stay allowed.

open_points.subject: working context lifecycle
open_points.text: none chosen, expired or withdrawn answers that there is none
open_points.question: Which action withdraws a working context, and who takes it? What happens to the context when its project is archived?
options: owner action 'clear the working context'; archiving the context's project withdraws it
only expiry or a new choice ends it
open_points.default_guess: Add the owner action 'clear the working context'. Archiving the context's project ends the context.

open_points.subject: switch request handling
open_points.text: a pending request the owner sees in the owner interface; the working context does not change
open_points.question: What are the owner's actions on a pending switch request (confirm, decline), and what does each output? Can several requests be pending? Is a request for an archived project refused? Does the agent learn the outcome?
options: confirm = choose that project; decline closes the request; one pending request at a time, a new one replaces it
many pending requests, each confirmed or declined
open_points.default_guess: Owner actions: confirm (makes the working context for that project) and decline. A new request replaces the pending one. An archived project is refused. Kernel reads the request's status.

open_points.subject: R0-32 working context cardinality
open_points.text: The choice makes a working context
open_points.question: Is there one working context for the whole instance, or one per agent or Kernel session? R0-25 says 'any language-model agent'.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Kernel's create and publish vs agent authority
open_points.text: create a project | owner; a service with a service token (today Cabinet Kernel)
open_points.question: Kernel's only Registry token carries agent authority, which is confined to the current working context. Can Kernel (the agent) still create a new project, which lies outside any context? Are Kernel's 'add a room' and publish calls confined to the context project? Does Kernel hold a second, non-agent token for its producer role?
options: agent authority may not create projects; only the owner creates
creating is allowed and the new project does not become the context
Kernel holds two tokens: producer and agent
open_points.default_guess: Only the owner creates projects. Kernel's room and publish calls are confined to the context project.

open_points.subject: R0-07 caller-supplied id in production vs R0-34
open_points.text: an id crosses into production only by an explicit import
open_points.question: Does 'create a project' with a caller-supplied `project_id` still exist on production, or does production only mint ids on create and accept foreign ids only through import?
options: production create always mints; supplied ids only via import
supplied ids still accepted on create in production
open_points.default_guess: On production, create always mints the id. A carried-over id enters only through import. Supplied ids on create stay a test-instance feature.

open_points.subject: import a project with its identity
open_points.text: the project under the identity it carries in its source
open_points.question: What is the source of an import: an export of another instance, the running v1 instances, a file? Which action produces it? Test instances have their own identity space and never share production's. Does an import from a test instance keep the test id or receive a production id? How does import fit R0-34's rule that test instances hold no production personal data, when migration brings customers in?
options: source is an export file from an instance; add an export action
source is a v1 instance read directly; only migration keeps its ids, test imports get a minted id
open_points.default_guess: The source is an export file made by an owner-only export action. Migrated v1 ids are kept. A project imported from a test instance receives a newly minted production id, recorded in the confirmed mapping.

open_points.subject: owner interface coverage
open_points.text: through the owner interface Registry serves (R0-29)
open_points.question: The Owner actor acts only through the owner interface. R0-29 lists project, customer, object, context, archive, audit and switch views. Does the interface also carry every other owner action: add a room, publish and withdraw a pointer, erase or restrict a customer, import?
options: the interface carries every owner action in the table
the owner uses some actions through another channel
open_points.default_guess: The owner interface carries every owner row of the primary actions table.

open_points.subject: hosts of PresuPro, Cabinet and Cabinet Kernel
open_points.text: the service API for services, reachable only on the production host and over the protected channel
open_points.question: Where do PresuPro, Cabinet and Cabinet Kernel run? R0-39's tunnel carries Portal only, so how do these services reach the production service API? Kernel serves the agent, and no agent runs on the home server: does Kernel run there?
options: all of them run on the home server
they run on the VPS and use the same WireGuard tunnel
each gets its own protected channel
open_points.default_guess: PresuPro, Cabinet and Kernel run on the home server and reach Registry locally. Only Portal uses the tunnel.

open_points.subject: onboard_object
open_points.text: a client of the API like any consumer, designed elsewhere; its staff-credential use ends with R0-30
open_points.question: Without the owner credential, and with no service token named for it in R0-27, can `onboard_object` call Registry at all? Is it retired or given its own token?
options: retired; its role moves to the owner interface and Kernel
keeps working with a service token of its own
open_points.default_guess: Retired. Remove it from the consumers.

open_points.subject: R0-27 Cabinet Web mirror
open_points.text: keeps its read only if it receives a token of its own
open_points.question: Does the Cabinet Web mirror receive a token? If it does, with which operations and which disclosure class?
options: no token; its read ends
a read-only token at business_confidential
open_points.default_guess: No token. The mirror's read ends.

open_points.subject: retention expiry and end of relationship
open_points.text: until the relationship with the customer ends, plus one year
open_points.question: The table has no action by which the owner records that a customer relationship ended. Which actor (the owner, or Registry on a schedule) carries out the erasure or anonymisation when a period expires?
options: owner action 'end relationship'; Registry erases on schedule
owner erases manually when reminded
open_points.default_guess: Add the owner action 'end a customer relationship'. Registry erases or anonymises on its own schedule and audits each erasure.
